glossary.Tick: One price update from the market.
glossary.Candle: One minute summarized as open, high, low, close and traded volume.
glossary.Parquet: A file format for storing table columns efficiently.
glossary.Contract: What a component promises to accept, return and own, independent of its internal code.
glossary.Interface: The named operations another component can call.
glossary.Signal: A trade suggestion with a symbol, side, quantity, price and decision time.
glossary.Fill: The quantity the broker says actually traded.
glossary.Reservation: Money or shares temporarily held for a pending order.
glossary.Reconciliation: Ask the broker what really happened and bring local account state into agreement.
glossary.Idempotency: Recognize a repeated request so a retry does not create a second order.
glossary.Backpressure: Slow incoming work when the next piece cannot keep up.
glossary.Atomic publication: Make a completed file visible in one step, so readers do not see half a file.
glossary.Paper trading: Simulate execution locally instead of placing a real broker order.
glossary.Dry run: Compute inference decisions but do not send them to execution.
glossary.Equity: Cash plus the current value of held shares.
glossary.Drawdown: The fall in account value from its previous high.
glossary.Registry: A list of named implementations that callers can choose from.
glossary.Fx: A Go library that supplies dependencies and starts/stops their lifecycle.
